newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita Elec to build Slovakia TV tuner plant.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita Elec to build Slovakia TV tuner plant.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Thursday that it plans to set up a television tuner plant in Slovakia in the autumn of 1997 to meet growing demand for television sets in the European market.

Matsushita Electric's director in charge of the European division, Seinosuke Kuraku, also said that Matsushita is in talks with the British Sky Broadcasting Group (BSkyB) over a possible stake in the company.
Kuraku, who was speaking at a news conference, did not provide any details.
"We are seeking a broadcasting partner in each area of the European market and BSkyB is one of many candidates," he said.
On the planned Slovakia plant, he said it would employ 800 people, adding that the company has not decided on the size of its investment.
Kuraku also said that the company expects a "reasonable" sales increase in the European market in 1997. "We expect another difficult year for us as the consumer electronics market is shrinking."
But he added that some manufacturers have stopped production of consumer electronics and competition has eased somewhat.
Kuraku was also asked what dollar/yen rate he would be comfortable with for Matsushita Electric's business.
"Somewhere in the area of 110 yen (to the dollar) could be the possibility," he told the news conference.

Kuraku also said that within three years Matsushita Electric aims for annual sales of 250 million German marks worth of broadcasting equipment, such as professional video cameras, in the European market.
He said the company has a 30 percent share of the broadcasting equipment market in Japan.
